description:
Fill the remaining sections of docs/verdict.md (defk-dtw.4) from the evidence:
- 'Should I use defk for X?': job-type guide (Elixir / defk / Nx / Rustler) from the workload rows and the NIF survey (defk-dtw.1), plus the traps list (poor_list_data, poor_tiny_calls, out_of_scope_word_count).
- Runtime contract: one row per promise (preemption, cleanup on process death, hot code upgrade, errors as exceptions) with linked test/bench and measured figure, the threat list (defk-5fc), and the never-take-down-the-BEAM evidence.
- Developer experience: the three-part bar with evidence (error catalogue, docs/language.md and its divergence page, the one rule consistent with every listed divergence: zero), plus the cold-test log.
- Limitations and what would change the verdict: one machine, cross-compiling, the C compiler stance (defk-dtw.11: elixir_make for apps, cc_precompiler-style for libraries, the mix release record), plus 'Where defk could grow' (expansion candidates from defk-dtw.5).
- Conclusion: a 3-5 sentence draft applying the pre-registered go/no-go rule; it may argue against the rule's outcome only explicitly.

Done when every section meets its bar from defk-dtw.4 and the draft is ready for the final session.

comments.text: Per review of wave 1: defk-ds0's evidence (packages gcc+libc6-dev minimum / build-essential, sizes, build times, runtime image needs no compiler) is in examples/release_debian/README.md and must be carried into the verdict's Runtime contract / Limitations; also defk-n8f (.so not shipped in releases).

Draft landed (2026-10-14). Every section of docs/verdict.md is filled; the conclusion applies the rule and comes out at 'grow into a library', with the frame that most NIFs wrap libraries and BIF-backed jobs lose. Ready for the final session (defk-sgw.6, human): accept or amend the conclusion, then close the map (defk-dtw).
